item.title: The Oscars’ Fight to Stay Relevant Amid Its Cultural Decline
item.description: Fragmented media, streaming and social media have weakened the Oscars’ cultural influence, prompting the Academy to chase audiences on YouTube.

item.title: Porsche’s New CEO Michael Leiters Outlines Turnaround Plan Amid Company ‘Crisis’
item.description: Three months into his role, Michael Leiters launches a sweeping plan to revive Porsche after falling profits and sales declines.

item.title: Garth Greenan’s Long Game: How the Dealer Is Redefining Artist Representation for the Future
item.description: Over 15 years, the dealer built a gallery around artists whose importance was hiding in plain sight. Now it's moving to Soho.

item.title: The 15 Weekender Bags for Men Who Travel With Intention
item.description: The mudroom has never looked this polished, from machine-washable workhorses to hand-woven Italian leather that costs more than the hotel.

item.title: Collector Jordan D. Schnitzer’s David Hockney Holdings Come Home to Portland
item.description: The traveling exhibition, which gathers 60 year's worth of drawings, collages, photographic works and more, showcases the artist's lifelong engagement with both tradition and innovation.

item.title: Meet the Collector: Karun Thakar’s Mission to Share the Hidden Histories of Indian Chintz
item.description: He has spent a lifetime collecting textiles from around the world in an effort to spotlight the overlooked makers behind abstract masterpieces he believes “the Western art world has always ignored.”

item.title: The Eighth Lights Up Chelsea With a Bar That Steals the Show
item.description: With an alabaster-glowing bar and conceptual rituals, The Eighth’s debut delivers on design, but its cocktail ceremonies are still a work in progress.

item.title: How Regulatory Fragmentation Is Reshaping A.I. Startups
item.description: LaunchLemonade’s Cien Solon examines how diverging A.I. regulations are reshaping the way startups are built. For founders navigating a fragmented regulatory landscape, she argues that embedding governance early can turn compliance into a strategic advantage rather than a constraint.

item.title: Rev. Jesse Jackson and Milton Friedman: The Unlikeliest Bedfellows in American Capitalism
item.description: The Ford Foundation’s Roy Swan reflects on the death of Rev. Jesse Jackson and a conviction he shared with libertarian economist Milton Friedman: that you cannot have credible democracy if large groups are structurally locked out. But, Swan argues, Jackson understood what Friedman did not: the lock doesn’t open by itself.

item.title: In Kochi, a Biennial Becomes a Civic Laboratory
item.description: The Kochi-Muziris Biennale showcases how major international exhibitions can transcend traditional displays of art, transforming ordinary spaces into vibrant hubs of reflection, experimentation, shared learning and empowerment.
